name: StarSling

free.conditions: No credit card; first month only; unused minutes do not roll over.

caveats: GitHub Actions/Review Runners, not always-on generic VM (engine classifies the "ci" regime as a CI runner, so non-CI workloads see it as a different kind of product; no alt flag). Ubuntu 24.04, 5th-gen AMD EPYC. Advertised unlimited concurrency; job/session maximum not verified.
GPU rates include 4 vCPU/16 GB/100 GB host, not add-on rates. GPU access requires contacting provider; H100 coming soon, excluded from numerical rate list.
Do not apply advertised performance/TFLOPS savings as universal wall-clock discounts.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
2,000 free runner minutes in the first month (no card; no rollover).

fleet.notes: CI/Review Runner product advertises unlimited concurrency, not a numerical resource guarantee. New signup includes 2,000 minutes without card. Numeric GPU allocation and large-fleet admission not published; GPU access may require contacting provider.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes. There is no reuse across jobs, no warm pool of shared runners, and nothing — filesystem, image cache, process, or credential — carries from one job to the next.
snapshot_auto.note: These are single-use, ephemeral GitHub Actions runners: no state is saved.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Your job's filesystem, including the checkout — destroyed with the machine. Nothing is copied off it.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The API and CLI are read-only CI analytics (runs, jobs, logs, why, time, usage, bill). There is no snapshot or checkpoint call. Caching is done through GitHub's actions/cache: 'StarSling operates no separate cache or artifact store.'

harness_api.quote: The StarSling control plane exposes an HTTP API for everything the platform knows about your CI: which runs and jobs executed, why one failed, where the wall-clock went, and what it all cost.
harness_api.note: StarSling's own 'AI agents' run on StarSling's side and open CI-optimization PRs; they are not a harness you drive inside the runner. The sling CLI is 'agent-first' only in the sense that coding agents can call it to read CI data. Nothing starts or streams Claude Code, Codex or similar inside a runner.

guest_firewall.note: Per the data-handling page, 'On our sandbox providers a CPU job runs in a microVM; on our EC2 fleet ... your job runs in a privileged container *on its own dedicated instance*'. GPU tiers are containers on a dedicated machine. As a drop-in ubuntu-latest replacement, the runner presumably has sudo (not stated explicitly), so iptables/nftables inside works.

secret_proxy.quote: The runner itself is our machine. Secrets are in memory and on disk on the VM while your job runs. What protects them there is that the machine is single-use and destroyed with the job, not that the values never arrived.
secret_proxy.note: GitHub injects Actions secrets straight into the runner as env vars. There is no credential-injecting proxy.
